scope: Primary-source research, not a completed installation or quality benchmark. No paid software, accounts, model access terms, or downloads were activated.

decision.cascadeur: Promising offline editing experiment for arms, support, center of mass and jump trajectories; Free cannot export a usable game interchange clip.
decision.kimodo: Promising separate text/constraint-to-motion source; prefer a controlled official SOMA v1.2 CLI trial because the documented G1 postprocessing is weak. The existing G1 adapter remains a comparison option. This kinematic model does not guarantee dynamic balance.
decision.bridge: Optional community convenience layer after a controlled CLI test; configure a separate G-drive environment and caches rather than accepting the default auto-installer.

cascadeur.classification: Proprietary commercial animation software with a free tier; not open-source software.
cascadeur.published_usd_faq_prices: Checked2026-10-29: Free0; Indie19/month or96/year; Pro49/month or396/year. Regional cards/currency may differ; no purchase was attempted.

plans.free: One user, non-commercial use, CASC-only export. Includes rigging, physics tools, inbetweening and animation unbaking.
plans.indie: Adds interchange export; comparison grid lists FBX, DAE, USD and GLTF. Aggregate gross revenue or funding must be below USD100,000/year.
plans.pro: Adds retargeting, environment interaction in AutoPhysics, scene linking and quadruped AutoPosing.

autoposing.facts: Predicts poses from manipulated controllers. Requires a standard Cascadeur rig; humanoids or quadrupeds, with quadrupeds restricted to Pro+. Quick Rigging maps body joints. The default setup can change the initial rest pose: preserve the original rig and work on copies.

autophysics.facts: Uses a center of mass and associated character geometry. A physical assistant proposes an edited motion that can be applied. A red assistant means a physically accurate solution is impossible under the current setup and poses/timing need manual changes. This is not guaranteed automatic balance.

blender_roundtrip.facts: Vendor recommends binary FBX for Blender. Do not enable Automatic Bone Orientation on import because it changes joint rotations. DAE is deprecated since Blender4.5; FBX is the practical first roundtrip for our Blender4.5.15. A paid export-capable plan is required.

hardware.facts: Vendor minimum: 4GB RAM, 64-bit multicore CPU with SSE4.1, OpenGL4.1 GPU. Recommendation: 8GB RAM, faster CPU with AVX. Windows11 is supported. Our recorded RTX4090/96GB machine is comfortably above these listed requirements; actual scene performance has not been measured.

hands.facts: Finger AutoPosing expects five fingers with three joints each. Robot hand topology must be checked separately; preserve the authored finger shapes rather than assuming a valid mapping.

kimodo.repo_facts: Official NVIDIA kinematic motion diffusion model with text, full-body keyframes, end-effector, root-path and waypoint constraints. Code uses Apache2.0; model weights use separate licenses. SOMA-RP-v1.2 was released October15,2026. G1-RP-v1 is also available. SMPLX-RP-v1 uses the separate NVIDIA R&D Model license, so it is not the default route for this shareable/game experiment.

license.facts: SOMA/G1 RP weights are listed under NVIDIA Open Model License. It permits commercial use subject to its terms; NVIDIA does not claim ownership of outputs, and outputs are not derivative models. Redistribution of models has separate notice/agreement requirements. Third-party dependencies and the gated text encoder retain their own terms.

setup.facts: Primarily developed/tested on Linux. Official instructions recommend a new environment and GPU PyTorch>2. Text encoding requires access to gated meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct plus a HuggingFace token. Account access has not been requested or assumed.

hardware.facts: Approximately17GB VRAM for entirely-GPU local generation; TEXT_ENCODER_DEVICE=cpu reduces GPU use below3GB with slower encoding. RTX4090 is among tested GPUs. Our24GB4090 appears suitable for an isolated inference trial; this is an inference from vendor requirements, not a local measurement. The17GB figure is VRAM, not download size. Exact disk/model-cache size must be enumerated before installation.

limitations.facts: Maximum10seconds per prompt; keep each prompt to one or two behaviors. Use fewer than20 constrained frames per constraint type except dense2D root paths. Multi-prompt transitions consume part of the following prompt. Raw motions may footskate or miss constraints; postprocessing helps but currently does not work well for the G1 skeleton.

skeletons.facts: Separate models target SOMA, G1 or SMPL-X. SOMA predicts30core joints and exports77joints; most hand/finger detail is absent internally. G1 has34learning joints including toes, removed from downstream qpos exports. Uniform training proportions mean our three bodies still require retargeting and geometry checks.

formats.facts: NPZ preserves joints, rotations, contacts and actual root trajectory. G1 CSV is36values: xyz, wxyz quaternion,29hinges, z-up/+X-forward MuJoCo coordinates. SOMA BVH exports77joints and scales metres to centimetres; its rest-pose option must match our adapter. These coordinate/unit conventions need explicit roundtrip validation.

community_blender_bridge.manifest_facts: Manifest declares v1.5.8, Blender>=4.2 and SPDX GPL-2.0-or-later. The README-linked LICENSE file returned404 at review. This is a community add-on, not NVIDIA's official Blender integration.
community_blender_bridge.readme_facts: Runs an external Python process rather than loading PyTorch into Blender. Author reports tests on Blender4.4/5.1; our4.5.15 meets the manifest minimum but is not locally tested. Auto-install creates ~/.kimodo-venv, uses Aero-Ex's offline fork and defaults to SOMA-RP-v1. Bone AutoMatch is fuzzy and still needs reviewed mappings/rest poses. Manual Python-environment selection is supported.
community_blender_bridge.local_policy: Default home-directory environment/HuggingFace caches can consume C:. A future trial should use a separate G-drive venv plus HF_HOME and package caches explicitly on G:, leaving the existing MotionBricks environment and Blender Python intact. Prefer a pinned official Kimodo CLI first.

local_inspection.limits: This is a targeted workspace/cache search, not proof that no unrelated system-wide installation exists.

proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.name: Offline physics cleanup
proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.input: Copied user-owned EVA rig and existing CC0 run/crouch/jump clips; retain originals and current contact masks.
proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.experiment: Compare unchanged clip with manually reviewed arms/CoM/AutoPhysics edits. Free permits in-app assessment; an export-capable license is needed for a game roundtrip.
proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.measure: World heel/toe drift during trusted stance, floor/contact geometry, takeoff extension, flight timing, landing knee flexion, arm balance and before/after reviewer scores. A support-polygon/CoM plot is diagnostic, not proof of dynamic stability.

proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.name: Official Kimodo clip source
proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.input: Three4-6second prompts: crouch walk, run-and-forward-jump, sidestep; two seeds each, with optional sparse user-owned pose targets.
proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.experiment: Prefer current SOMA-RP-v1.2 via the official CLI, with reviewed BVH retargeting. Compare raw and postprocessed output; optionally compare G1 CSV through the existing adapter, noting the documented weak G1 postprocessing.
proposed_small_tests_not_yet_run.measure: Record seed/model/version/license, generation time/VRAM, constraint error, trusted-stance foot drift, floor/self-intersection review, three-body rig/export parity and scores. Preserve native outputs separately from contact/controller edits.

role_inference: Use consistent CC0 clips as a baseline, Kimodo for semantic clip ideas, Cascadeur for offline animation editing, MotionBricks for target/state transitions, and explicit game-side contacts/obstacle/speed logic for the reactive course. These tools complement each other; generated pose sequences alone do not provide a physical character controller.
